newsitem.title: USA: Urologix says FDA finds T3 PMA suitable.
newsitem.headline: Urologix says FDA finds T3 PMA suitable.

text.p: Urologix Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration completed an initial review of the company's pre-market approval application for its Targeted Transurethral Thermo-ablation Therapy system for treating enlarged prostate disease or benign prostatic hyperplasia
The company said the FDA found the application suitable for filing and said it would not to be referred to an FDA advisory panel for review and recommendation.
Chief Executive Jack Meyer said, "This is a positive indication that our efforts to obtain the regulatory approval necessary for marketing the T3 System in the important U.S. market remain on track."
As a result, he said, Urologix is refining its U.S. marketing strategy.

"Once approved, we plan to reach the estimated 7,500 urologists who treat BPH patients in the U.S. through a direct sales force. In addition, Jack Costello, our recently appointed executive vice president for sales and marketing, is actively recruiting to build the domestic sales management infrastructure necessary to launch the T3 System after FDA commercial marketing approval has been achieved," Meyer said.
The company's Japanese distribution partner received approval to market the T3 in that country in February. The device was approved for European marketing last July.
The company's global distributor for markets other than the United States and Japan is Boston Scientific Corp.
Urologix, public since May, lost $1.6 million in its second quarter ended December 31 on sales of $1.3 million, compared to a year-ago loss of $1.7 million on sales of $182,875.
